extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in film (fans, journalists, researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia film article summarizing a single film's production, release, reception, box office performance, and related impacts. Includes quantitative reception metrics, awards, and economic effects cited in prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office gross (domestic, international, worldwide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dark Waters has grossed more than $11.1 million in the United States and Canada, and $11.9 million in other countries, for a worldwide total of over $23.1 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page provides breakdowns by region (US & Canada vs other countries) and a summed worldwide total. Used as a measure of commercial performance; figures are given as reported totals with citation to Box Office Mojo/IMDb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening weekend per-venue average
rubrics_metrics.description: Its opening weekend, the film made $102,656 from four theaters, a per-venue average of $25,651.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-venue (per-theater) average on limited release is used to indicate early demand/market strength prior to expansion. The article cites the raw opening gross, number of theaters, and resulting per-venue average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical expansion and subsequent weekend grosses
rubrics_metrics.description: The film expanded to 94 theaters the following weekend, making $630,000. It went wide its third weekend (2,012 theaters), making $4.1 million, and then $1.9 million its fourth weekend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The progression of theater counts and weekend grosses across release weeks is reported as evidence of box-office trajectory over time (limited→wide) and momentum or drop-off after expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes critics' percentage and critical consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: On Rotten Tomatoes, 89% of 236 critics' reviews of the film are positive, with an average rating of 7.3/10; the site's critical consensus reads, 'Dark Waters powerfully relays a real-life tale of infuriating malfeasance, honoring the victims and laying blame squarely at the feet of the perpetrators.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotten Tomatoes provides both the percentage of positive reviews and an average numeric rating; the site also gives a short 'critical consensus' blurb which the article quotes as an encapsulation of critics' qualitative judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic weighted average score and qualitative label
rubrics_metrics.description: On Metacritic, the film has a weighted average score of 73 out of 100, based on reviews from 38 critics, indicating 'generally favorable' reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metacritic's numeric weighted average and its mapping to qualitative bands (e.g., 'generally favorable') are used as an aggregated critical-evaluation metric; the article cites both the score and the label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience polling (CinemaScore and PostTrak)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave the film an average grade of 'A−' on an A+ to F scale, while PostTrak gave it an average of 3.5 out of 5 stars, with 60% saying they would definitely recommend it to a friend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience-reaction surveys (CinemaScore letter grade; PostTrak star rating and 'definitely recommend' percentage) are reported as measures of general-audience reception rather than critics' views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolades, nominations, and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The film received nominations and some wins across various awards bodies (e.g., nominations at Women in Film Critics Circle Awards, Satellite Awards; won Environmental Media Awards; listed nominations/wins in a table of accolades). The article also notes that many outlets felt the film was snubbed by the 92nd Academy Awards and 77th Golden Globe Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and nominations (counts, categories, winners vs nominees) are presented as qualitative markers of industry/peer recognition; the article lists specific awards, dates, categories, recipients, and results where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic/market impact on implicated companies
rubrics_metrics.description: The article reports that DuPont's stock price dropped after the film's release (a drop of 7.15 points on release day) and discusses related investor concerns and litigation impacts on spun-off companies (e.g., Chemours and 3M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stock-price movement and corporate statements are used to indicate the film's perceived economic or reputational impact on companies depicted. The article cites specific price changes, executive reactions, and subsequent corporate/legal developments as context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release strategy (limited release then wide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus Features gave Dark Waters a limited theatrical release on November 22, 2019, before releasing it wide on December 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distribution pattern (dates for premiere, limited release, and wide release) is documented and is relevant to interpreting box-office numbers and per-theater averages; release platform notes (e.g., later Netflix Canada release) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis in real reporting and source material
rubrics_metrics.description: The film is based on the 2016 New York Times Magazine article 'The Lawyer Who Became DuPont's Worst Nightmare' by Nathaniel Rich, and the article cites other investigative reporting and a memoir as source material for the film's story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provenance/credibility of the film's narrative is established by citing original journalism, books, and memoirs. The article lists these sources (NYT Magazine piece, investigative articles, book, memoir) as the factual basis for the dramatization, which can be used to assess claims of factual accuracy or fidelity.
